rows.speaker: هم
rows.claim: They identify the response to the oath as the statement that all the messengers were denied, at 38:14.
rows.anchor: فيزعمون ان موضع القسم في قوله {إن كل إلا كذب الرسل}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lat is treated like laysa, with its subject suppressed; lat occurs only with ḥīn.
rows.anchor: فشبهو {لات} ب {ليس} واضمروا فيها اسم الفاعل ولا تكون {لات} إلا مع "حين"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some raise ḥīn and parse lat like laysa, as though it meant there is no one, with the predicate suppressed.
rows.anchor: ورفع بعضهم {ولات حين مناص} فجعله في قوله مثل {ليس} كأنه قال " ليس أحد" واضمر الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses genitive awān after omitting ḥīn and attaching it to awān, since lat takes ḥīn.
rows.anchor: فجر "أوان" وحذف وأمضر "الحين" واضاف الى "أوان" لأن {لات} لا تكون الا مع "الحين"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the question as a construction like asking whether someone would make a hundred witnesses one witness.
rows.anchor: كما تقول: "اتجعل مئة شاهد شاهدا واحدا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording has no expressed predicate; its sense is whether one who shields himself from punishment is better than one who does not.
rows.anchor: فهذا لم يظهر له خبر في اللفظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the phrase is accusative because the preceding statement about setting out every kind of example in the Qur'an is definite and its predicate is accusative.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله {ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذاالقرآن من كل مثل} [27] معرفة فانتصب خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular relative pronoun is used with a plural sense, like man.
rows.anchor: فجعل "الذي" في معنى جماعة بمنزلة {من}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses wajūhuhum muswaddah as a nominative independent subject.
rows.anchor: وقال {وجوههم مسودة} فرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some put wajūhahum in the accusative and parse it as an appositional substitute.
rows.anchor: ونصب بعضهم فجعلها على البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four days include the previous two; he compares it to saying he married one woman yesterday and two today, counting yesterday's woman.
rows.anchor: فانما يعني ان هذا مع الأول اربعة ايام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase We enjoined the human concerning his parents means that We enjoined him to do good.
rows.anchor: قال {ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه} يقول: "بخير"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the accusative, sawāʾ is a verbal noun, as if the wording were istiwāʾ.
rows.anchor: فجعله مصدرا كأنه قال "استواء"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A genitive reading makes sawāʾ a noun describing the days as complete.
rows.anchor: وقد قرىء بالجر وجعل اسما للمستويات أي: في أربعة أيام تامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes ḥifẓan as an implied we protected it with protection; adorning the sky with lamps already implies tending and protecting it.
rows.anchor: قد أخبر أنه نظر في امرها وتعاهدها فذا يدل على الحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-quwā is the plural of quwwa; he compares it with dialectal plural pairs such as ḥabwa/ḥuban and rashwa/rashan.
rows.anchor: جماعة "القوة" وبعض العرب يقول "حبوة" و"حبى" فينبغي أن يقول "القوى"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs use two forms of the plural ṣuwar; he identifies one as the better form and cites the Qur'anic wording, while noting another reading.
rows.anchor: وبعض العرب يقول "صور" و"صور" والجيدة "صور"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some pronounce al-Lāt with a final h when pausing; similarly, Manāt becomes Manāh at pause.
rows.anchor: فاذا سكت قلت "اللاة" وكذلك "مناة" تقول "مناه"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some derive al-Lāt from the verb meaning to knead or mix, explaining it as the one who does that.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم {اللات} جعله [172 ب] من "اللات": الذي يلت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs pause with t on words written with tāʾ marbūṭa; Qur'anic words written with tāʾ are likewise stopped on with t, as in these examples.
rows.anchor: ولغة للعرب يسكتون على ما فيه الهاء بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An lā taziru is an appositional substitute for the phrase about what is in Moses' scriptures, meaning that no bearer bears another's burden.
rows.anchor: فقوله {أن لا تزر} بدل من قوله {بما في صحف موسى} [36]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural verb yahdūnanā agrees with bashar because the word has a collective sense.
rows.anchor: فجمع لأن "البشر" في المعنى جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means to retain or take in: one says an ear retained it, my hearing retained it, and I stored provisions or belongings; an unattributed al-Basīṭ line uses awʿaytu of storing provisions.
rows.anchor: الشر أخبث ما أوعيت من زاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafkhatan is accusative because the action falls on the blowing itself and no nominative noun precedes it.
rows.anchor: لأن الفعل وقع على النفخة اذا لم يكن قبلها اسم مرفوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of arjāʾihā is ar-rajā, a noun with a short final alif.
rows.anchor: وقال {والملك على أرجآئها} وواحدها "الرجا" وهو مقصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He derives ghislīn, with some uncertainty, from ghusl by adding yāʾ and nūn, like ʿifrīn and kifrīn.
rows.anchor: "الغسل" وزاد الياء والنون [177 ب] بمنزلة "عفرين" و"كفرين"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the accusative analysis, nazzāʿatan is an appositional substitute for the pronoun, and it is the predicate of inna.
rows.anchor: نصب على البدل من الهاء** وخبر "إن" {نزاعة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, laẓā may be nominative as the predicate of inna, with an-nazzāʿa nominative as a new subject.
rows.anchor: وان شئت جعلت {لظى} رفعا على خبر {إن} ورفعت "النزاعة" على الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān is grammatically singular but denotes people collectively, as shown by the plural exception except those who pray.
rows.anchor: فجعل {الإنسان} جميعا ويدلك على ذلك انه قد استثنى منه جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares the construction with asking what is the matter with someone standing, as in mā laka qāʾiman.
rows.anchor: كما تقول "ما لك قائما"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of ʿizīn is ʿizza, like thuba with the plural thibīn.
rows.anchor: وواحدة "العزين": العزة. مثل "ثبة" و"ثبين".

words: أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِّنَ الْجِنِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first anna is opened because it is the content of the revelation; he then considers the following clause about the Lord's majesty.
rows.anchor: على الابتداء اذا كان من كلام الجن فان فتح جعله على الوحي وهو حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the following clause is the jinn's speech, it begins independently; opening anna instead attaches it to the revelation, which he calls a good analysis.
rows.anchor: على الابتداء اذا كان من كلام الجن فان فتح جعله على الوحي وهو حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of shuhuban is shihāb.
rows.anchor: وقال {وشهبا} وواحدها: الشهاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the verb as testing; some Arabs say aftanahu instead of fatanahu in this sense.
rows.anchor: لأنك تقول "فتنته" وبعض العرب يقول "أفتنه" فتلك على تلك اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safara is the plural of sāfir, patterned like kafara from kāfir.
rows.anchor: وواحدهم "السافر" مثل "الكافر" و"الكفرة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of barrara is bārr, and barrara is a collective plural of abrār.
rows.anchor: وواحدهم "البار" و"البررة" جماعة "الأبرار"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes mā akfarahu as an exclamation: How ungrateful the human is.
rows.anchor: معناه على وجهين، قال بعضهم "على التعجب"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes mā akfarahu as a question meaning what made him disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "أي شيء أكفره"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the wording with the equivalent expression hadāhu al-ṭarīq, illustrating the relation between the path and the person guided.
rows.anchor: تقول "الطريق هداه" أي: "هداه الطريق"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read ʿadalaka with a lighter form; he glosses the phrase as God having formed the person in this way.
rows.anchor: قال {فعدلك} أي: كذا خلقك، وبعضهم يخففها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the doubled form, God balanced the person's parts against one another, making him proportionate; this has the same sense as ʿadalaka.
rows.anchor: فمن ثقل {عدلك} فانما يقول "عدل خلقك" و"عدلك" أي: عدل بعضك ببعضك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjacent identical kāf consonants may assimilate; he also describes when to leave them unassimilated according to whether the first or second letter is vowelled.
rows.anchor: فادغمت لأنهما حرفان مثلان. والمثلان يدغم احدهما في صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes yawm as a time adverb, meaning at a time when no soul controls anything for another, and connects it with the question about the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: فجعل اليوم حينا كأنه حين قال {ومآ أدراك ما يوم الدين} [17]

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some parse this as an explanation of the first mention of the day, as though it said: it is a day when no soul controls anything.
rows.anchor: فجعله تفسيرا لليوم الأول كأنه قال: "هو يوم لا تملك".
